chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Harun ibn Harizah from Shu'ayb from Isa ibn Hasan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I was with him when a cricket approached, so he said, 'Remove it, for it is a husk/shell from the chaff of the Fire.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the cricket in Shia hadith regarding ritual purity?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the cricket as a 'husk from the chaff of the Fire,' linking it to the concept of *Dabbat al-Ard* (the Beast of the Earth) or specific creatures signifying divine signs. This classification underscores the Shia scholarly view that certain insects possess unique spiritual statuses or serve as omens within the cosmic order of creation.
